newsitem.title: CHINA: China to tighten control of mineral resources.
newsitem.headline: China to tighten control of mineral resources.

text.p: China's mining firms will be forced to pay for the right to explore and exploit under new rules that take effect on January 1 and which aim to introduce market forces into the sector, state media said on Friday.

Miners given the right to explore and exploit mineral resources will have to pay an annual fee under amendments to the Mineral Resources Law, the China Daily quoted Vice Premier Zhou Jiahua as telling a conference in Beijing.
The fees would prevent mining companies from holding those rights virtually indefinitely, he said.
In the past, mining firms acquired such rights free of charge and because they suffered no losses from not making use of the rights, mineral resources they controlled could not be exploited, he said.
The amendments also allow the legal transfer of mining rights, a move aimed at attracting both domestic and overseas investment to the cash-strapped mining sector, Zhou said.

Other measures to guarantee state ownership include continued collection of compensation fees from mining companies to fund protection of mineral resources, creating a unified national planning agency and improving supervision, Zou said.

He cited problems resulting from localities and mining enterprises assuming that mineral resources belonged to the place and people who discovered them, and stressed that all resources were administered by the central government.

Relaxations of state controls following the introduction of economic reform in 1978 have triggered a rush to develop the mining industry, with unregulated, small-scale coal and gold mines appearing in many areas.
